title: Rav Nachman bar Ami
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Eruvin 66a in Hyman’s citation. At the matching [Eruvin 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.67a.14) he speaks ‘in the name of Ulpana’ (משמיה דאולפנא).

Hyman reports that [Seder HaDorot, under Ulpana](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=263&lang=en) (אולפני), reads Rav Chanin bar Ami, and that [Dikdukei Soferim](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/-tMwzyO-dBEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA272) reads R’ Chanin bar Ami, “in the name of Ilfi” (משמיה דאילפי).
Hyman also reports that, according to the Arukh’s reading of [Moed Katan 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.22b.21), Rav Chisda spoke to Rav Nachman bar Ami.[^4]

notes.text: Ulpana may be a name or a term for teaching/school; the alternative Ilfi and the Seder HaDorot heading Ulpanei are preserved. Seder HaDorot has Rav Chanin, while Dikdukei Soferim is cited with the shorter title Rabbi.

The saved whole Davidson Eruvin67a scalar explicitly has Rav Nachman bar Ami in the name of Ulpana, beside supplied66a. It does not decide whether Ulpana is a personal name, teacher or school, nor prove a vav/zayin print error. SederHaDorot’s Chanin reading was only a discovery snippet and DikdukeiSoferim was not fetched; both remain Hyman’s reports. Full Rav Chanin in the former remains distinct from abbreviated R' Chanin in the latter; older full Rabbi wording is withdrawn additively. MoedKatan22b’s Arukh reading remains attributed, with same-notice Nachman completion but no new authority identity.

The consulted Eruvin 67a names Rav Nachman bar Ami and Ulpana. The sentence continues on 67b with “even if it opens into an enclosure.” Seder HaDorot 263:1 has the abbreviated opening א״ר and names Chanin bar Ami and Ulpana. Dikdukei Soferim, p. 272, gives Chanin bar Ami and Ilfi in its manuscript column beside Nachman and Ulpana in the printed column. The consulted Moed Katan 22b has Rav Chisda speak to Rav Chanan bar Rava in the mourning episode. The Arukh variant remains Hyman’s report.

The printed and manuscript columns of [Dikdukei Soferim, p. 272](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/-tMwzyO-dBEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA272) display Nachman/Ulpana and Chanin/Ilfi respectively. The Eruvin statement continues at the [start of 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.67b.1). The linked Moed Katan text names Rav Chanan bar Rava as the addressee. Hyman attributes the reading Rav Nachman bar Ami to the Arukh.
